title: Broker fees and London budgets
summary: Eight energy intermediaries checked. None of the pages reviewed publishes a fixed siteworks arrangement fee. Obtain an itemised quote. The eight London figures below estimate the underlying work only, using published provider prices or a clearly labelled UK guide proxy.
caution: Supplier, network and meter-owner charges are separate from a broker's arrangement fee or energy-contract commission. No broker markup or London premium has been invented. A missing published fee does not mean the service is free.

tpis.name: Bionic
tpis.charging: General brokerage is paid through supplier commission included in the energy rates. Its terms normally provide for no direct customer service fee, with exceptions and a right to introduce charges after notification. Its meter guide says installation prices depend on meter type and work required.
tpis.context: The general brokerage terms do not establish a £0 siteworks installation price. Request the installation cost and any separate arrangement fee.
tpis.vat: No fixed siteworks fee or VAT basis published on the reviewed pages.

sources.title: Bionic terms, clauses 5.1 to 5.3
sources.quote: there is no fee due from a Customer to Bionic for providing the Services

tpis.name: Love Energy Savings
tpis.charging: Customers do not normally pay LOVE directly for brokerage. Supplier commission is usually an uplift in the unit rate. Some suppliers instead pay a fixed fee when new meters are installed, but no amount is published.
tpis.context: Its published example is 1p/kWh × 25,000 kWh/year × two years = £500 estimated energy-contract commission. This is an illustration, not a meter installation or siteworks tariff.
tpis.vat: VAT basis not stated for the commission illustration; not a customer siteworks invoice.

sources.title: LOVE commission and fee transparency
sources.quote: Some suppliers may instead pay a fixed fee, for example, when new meters are installed.

tpis.name: Utility Helpline
tpis.charging: Tendering is normally free unless otherwise agreed. Commission generally comes from the supplier and may be built into unit rates or standing charges. The amount is disclosed individually before the contract. Its new-connections service coordinates suppliers, distributors and metering providers.
tpis.context: September 2026 disclosure illustrates 0.50p/kWh × 10,000 kWh/year = £50/year electricity commission, or £150 over three years. This example is not a siteworks fee.
tpis.vat: VAT basis not stated for the commission illustration; confirm the quote's VAT separately.

sources.title: Utility Helpline fees, September 2026
sources.quote: The amount of Commission is not the same for every Customer or Contract.

tpis.name: Omnium
tpis.charging: New connections are remunerated through a margin on the final unit rate or a fixed management fee, agreed in writing before signing. Siteworks are quoted per job before an appointment is raised.
tpis.context: The connections page expressly holds no prices. Request the broker management fee separately from the meter operator and network works.
tpis.vat: No fixed fee or VAT basis published on this page.

sources.title: Omnium new connections and meters
sources.quote: Site works are quoted per job before anything is raised. This page holds no prices.

tpis.name: Inspired
tpis.charging: Offers managed connections, disconnections, meter installation/removal, relocations, capacity changes and energisation. Its siteworks page directs customers to request a quote, without publishing a price or markup.
tpis.context: Project coordination is offered, but no fixed siteworks administration fee is available from the reviewed service page.
tpis.vat: No fixed fee or VAT basis published on this page.

sources.title: Inspired siteworks services
sources.quote: Request a quote to get started.

tpis.name: Utility Bidder
tpis.charging: Guide describes supplier-priced installations, with a £200 to £800 UK electricity estimate. Gas costs vary by meter and supplier. No broker arrangement fee shown.
tpis.context: Guide estimate of installation cost, not Utility Bidder's fee or a London quote.
tpis.vat: VAT inclusion is not stated for the £200 to £800 guide range.

sources.title: Utility Bidder business meter-installation guide, 30 March 2026
sources.type: TPI primary guide, not installer tariff
sources.quote: the average cost of having a new electric meter installed in the UK ranges between £200 and £800

tpis.name: Consultiv Utilities
tpis.charging: Its terms describe supplier-paid commission included in the energy unit price, with the level varying by supplier and set by Consultiv. Its service evidence includes metering and siteworks, without a fixed installation or arrangement price.
tpis.context: The published illustration is 0.5p/unit × 40,000 units/year × two years = £400 commission. This is energy procurement commission, not a siteworks charge. Contract-failure fees are also not siteworks charges.
tpis.vat: VAT basis not stated for the commission illustration.

sources.title: Consultiv terms, section 8
sources.quote: The timing and amount of the Commission Payment varies from Supplier to Supplier

sources.title: Consultiv metering and siteworks service evidence

tpis.name: Advantage Utilities
tpis.charging: Terms allow supplier-paid procurement fees; direct consultancy may use a fixed or time-based fee agreed in writing. The siteworks service offers project management and competitive quotes for meter installation and infrastructure.
tpis.context: No siteworks fee is published. The service-page 'No Fee' statement concerns a commercial energy audit and must not be read as free siteworks.
tpis.vat: No fixed siteworks fee or VAT basis published on the reviewed pages.

londonEstimates.area: UK Power Networks: London, South East and East of England
londonEstimates.basis: UKPN reports 65% of customers in this underground-cable band, 30% at £2,650 to £5,510 and 5% above £5,510. It is a regional historical-cost distribution, not a London-only average or fixed quote.
londonEstimates.context: Meter removal and broker arrangement fees are separate. Council permits and complex work can push the network quote above this band. Large supplies require a separate commercial quote.
londonEstimates.vat: Excludes VAT, explicitly stated by UKPN.

londonEstimates.job: Electricity meter installation, simple existing supply
londonEstimates.area: UK guide proxy for a London starting budget
londonEstimates.basis: Utility Bidder publishes £200 to £800 as a typical UK electricity meter-installation range. Used unchanged as a provisional London guide because no London-specific retail tariff was found. No London premium has been added.
londonEstimates.context: A broker's editorial guide, not its arrangement fee or a supplier price list. Existing supply assumed for budgeting; CT/half-hourly metering, network upgrades, new connections, civil works and broker fees need individual quotes. A supplier smart-meter replacement may have no upfront charge.
londonEstimates.vat: VAT inclusion not stated. Do not label this +VAT or VAT-inclusive without a supplier quote.

londonEstimates.customer: Home or small business; confirm package scope
londonEstimates.basis: Electrician247.London publishes £3,000–£8,000 as a realistic total depending on dig length, cable upgrade and metering arrangement. Its separate priced package for a single-to-three-phase DNO upgrade plus new board starts at £4,995 and lists DNO application, dig, cable, new metering and TP&N board. The narrative range and advertised package are distinct examples, not a fixed tariff.
londonEstimates.context: Provisional London planning estimate, not a confirmed market minimum or maximum. The provider works with homes and small commercial sites. Confirm exact network, supplier-metering, internal-board and broker-arrangement inclusions in an itemised quote. A TPI fee is separate and unpublished; no fixed arrangement-fee range is evidenced. Complex reinforcement or civil works can exceed this guide range.
londonEstimates.vat: VAT basis not stated on the contractor page; confirm with the provider.

methodology: Primary provider terms, disclosures, service pages and network or meter-owner schedules were checked online on 1 October 2026. Not publicly published means no fixed siteworks arrangement price was found on these reviewed pages, not proof that a private tariff does not exist. Illustrative energy-contract commissions are not market averages or siteworks fees. London budgets retain the source's geographic and job scope. They are never assigned to a particular intermediary and exclude any unknown intermediary margin. The lower-confidence electricity meter proxy is a UK broker guide, not an installer tariff. VAT is marked only as stated in the relevant source.
